notices.title: Storm-2570 post-compromise remote access and service discovery behavior
notices.observation_context: Microsoft reports tracking this actor since April 2025, but the cited research does not establish a first calendar date for each behavior.

prerequisites.description: Corroborated post-compromise RDP, SMB, or remote-management behavior is observed in the asset context.

attack_mappings.rationale: The source reports NetScan or Nmap service discovery; apply this mapping only when that specific behavior is observed.

detection: Correlate authenticated RDP, SMB, remote-management, process, and endpoint telemetry after a confirmed compromise.
Look for observed NetScan or Nmap activity before applying the T1046 mapping.
remediation: Contain the confirmed compromise under the incident-response plan and review remote-access credentials and tooling.
defensive.safe_applicability: This is a behavior notice, not a vulnerability notice. Microsoft reported post-compromise behavior and explicitly left initial access unconfirmed.
defensive.safe_next_action: Validate the observed post-compromise behavior and its timeline with endpoint and authentication evidence; do not infer initial access from an exposed RDP or SMB service.

limitations: The source does not establish RDP, SMB, or remote-management software as an initial access point or vulnerability.
The source does not provide an affected-version allowlist, so this record remains unknown in automated asset assessment and cannot become a candidate.
An open port or enabled service alone is not campaign attribution or evidence of compromise.

notices.title: Dell RecoverPoint for VMs CVE-2026-22769
notices.observation_context: Google reports observed exploitation since at least mid-2024; the cited sources do not establish an exact first exploitation date or the initial access vector.

prerequisites.description: The asset context establishes the RecoverPoint appliance Tomcat Manager configuration and the advisory's hard-coded credential risk context.

attack_mappings.rationale: The incident research reports lateral movement by exploiting a RecoverPoint for VMs appliance; apply this mapping only when lateral exploitation of the scoped appliance is independently observed.

detection: Identify the exact RecoverPoint for VMs product and version, then review Tomcat Manager access and appliance authentication telemetry.
remediation: Follow Dell DSA-2026-079's version-specific path to 6.0.3.1 HF1 or its remediation script, or the DSA-2026-096 path to 6.1; verify applied remediation and restrict management reachability while pending.
defensive.safe_applicability: Applicability is limited to the explicitly allowlisted Dell RecoverPoint for VMs releases with reachable and configured Tomcat Manager context.
defensive.safe_next_action: Confirm the appliance inventory and configuration, then open a targeted investigation against the Dell advisory using authorized product-specific procedures.

limitations: A candidate is not a vulnerability or exploitability finding.
This notice does not apply to arbitrary Linux systems or unrelated Apache Tomcat installations.
Tomcat Manager reachability without exact product, version, and configuration evidence is insufficient.
The exact-version allowlist covers Dell's named releases; other legacy and patch levels remain unknown even where Dell describes a broader affected range.
A remediation script may address the issue without changing the version string; this matcher cannot verify that script or a patch's installation.

notices.title: Apple Screen Sharing CVE-2026-65400
notices.observation_context: The cited Apple advisory and original research do not establish exploitation in the wild or an exact first observation date.

prerequisites.description: Screen Sharing is confirmed enabled in the asset configuration.

attack_mappings.rationale: The original research describes unauthorized access through reachable Screen Sharing; apply this mapping only when exploitation for lateral movement between hosts is independently observed.

detection: Inventory the exact macOS Tahoe and Screen Sharing versions and confirm whether Screen Sharing is enabled and reachable.
remediation: Update macOS Tahoe to 26.6.1 or later as directed by Apple and disable or restrict Screen Sharing when it is not required.
defensive.safe_applicability: Applicability requires explicitly allowlisted Tahoe 26.5.2 or 26.6 context plus enabled and reachable Screen Sharing.
defensive.safe_next_action: Verify the exact OS and Screen Sharing configuration, then follow Apple's update guidance.

limitations: A candidate is not a vulnerability or exploitability finding.
Other macOS versions remain unknown unless a primary source explicitly adds them.
Service reachability without exact product, version, and enabled-state evidence is insufficient.
